title: Chocolate Factory
subtitle: From cocoa bean to wrapped bar
summary: A complete bean-to-bar line: roast, winnow, grind, conche, temper, deposit, cool and wrap — and why chocolate must be tempered to snap.
overview: A chocolate bar starts as the bitter seed of a tropical fruit. Fermented and dried on the farm, cocoa beans arrive at the factory hard and sour. Eight machines, working one after another, turn them into the glossy bar that snaps cleanly and melts on your tongue.

Heat does most of the work. The roaster develops flavour; the melanger's granite rollers grind nibs so fine — under 20 micrometres — that the tongue cannot feel the particles; the conche stirs warm chocolate for hours to drive off sharp acids and coat every grain of sugar in cocoa butter.

The cleverest step is tempering. Cocoa butter can crystallise in six different forms, and only Form V gives gloss and snap. The tempering machine melts every crystal, cools the chocolate to seed new ones, then warms it just enough to melt all but Form V. Slide the working temperature and watch what goes wrong when it is out of the window.

controls.label: Working temperature
controls.help: The temperature the chocolate is held at after seeding. Keep it inside the Form V window.

controls.label: Roast temperature
controls.help: Hotter roasts darken the beans and push flavour from fruity to roasty.

controls.label: Line speed
controls.help: Each mould holds four 100 g bars.

steps.title: Roasting
body: Fermented beans tumble in a gas-heated drum at 110–150 °C for 15 to 40 minutes. Sugars and amino acids react (the Maillard reaction), creating hundreds of flavour compounds and the familiar chocolate aroma.
A rotating sieve in front cools the batch quickly so the roast stops exactly where the roaster wants it. Try the roast slider: the sight glass and the cooled beans darken as the temperature rises.

steps.title: Cracking & winnowing
body: The roasted beans are cracked into pieces called nibs. A stream of air from the blower lifts away the light, papery shells, while the heavier nibs fall through.
A cyclone on top spins the air so the shells drop out into the bin — they become garden mulch or animal feed — and the clean nibs travel on to the grinder.

steps.title: Grinding
body: In the melanger two granite rollers roll round a granite bed. Nibs are about half fat (cocoa butter), so as they are crushed they melt into a thick, dark liquid called cocoa liquor.
Sugar and, for milk chocolate, milk powder are added from the hoppers above. Grinding continues until particles are below about 20 micrometres — smaller than the tongue can detect.

steps.title: Conching
body: The conche stirs and kneads the warm chocolate, 10 to 18 hours depending on the recipe. Aeration drives off volatile acids and water, and friction coats every particle in cocoa butter.
The result is smoother, mellower and more liquid. The name comes from the shell shape of the first trough, invented by Rodolphe Lindt in 1879.

steps.title: Tempering
body: Cocoa butter can set in six crystal forms. Only Form V is glossy, snaps cleanly and melts just below body temperature. The tempering machine first melts all crystals at 45–50 °C, then cools the chocolate to seed new ones, then warms it to the working temperature, which melts every form except V.

Each chocolate has its own window: about 31–32 °C for dark, 29–30 °C for milk and 28–29 °C for white, because milk fat interferes with the crystals. Too warm and the seeds melt: the bars bloom grey and soft. Too cool and unstable crystals thicken the chocolate.

steps.title: Depositing
body: A piston depositor fills every cavity of each mould with an exact dose, here 100 g per bar, four bars per mould. The moulds are polished polycarbonate, so each bar takes a mirror shine from them.
The moulds are shaken as they move on, which brings air bubbles to the surface so the bars have no holes.

steps.title: Cooling
body: The filled moulds ride through a tunnel chilled to about 12 °C. As Form V crystals grow, the chocolate contracts slightly, which is what lets the bars drop out of the moulds.
Cooling too fast or too cold causes condensation and sugar bloom, so the tunnel controls temperature and humidity along its length.

steps.title: Wrapping
body: Moulds are turned over and tapped; the bars fall out and the empty moulds return under the line. A flow wrapper folds gold foil and a paper sleeve around each bar.
The wrapped bars are counted into cartons. Store them at 15–18 °C: warmer, and cocoa butter migrates to the surface as fat bloom.

parts.name: Cocoa bean sacks
parts.role: Fermented, sun-dried beans arrive from the farm in 60 kg jute sacks.

parts.name: Roasting drum
parts.role: A perforated steel drum that turns over a gas burner so every bean roasts evenly.

parts.name: Gas burner
parts.role: Heats the air flowing through the drum; its window glows hotter with the roast setting.

parts.name: Roaster cabinet
parts.role: Holds the burner, the drum drive and the controls.

parts.name: Bean hopper
parts.role: Holds the next batch of raw cocoa beans, dropped into the drum all at once.

parts.name: Cooling sieve
parts.role: A rotating tray with a stirring arm that cools freshly roasted beans in minutes.

parts.name: Chimney
parts.role: Carries away the roasting smoke and moisture.

parts.name: Winnower
parts.role: Cracks the beans and blows away the shells with a stream of air.

parts.name: Cyclone separator
parts.role: Spins the air so the light shells drop out of it.

parts.name: Air blower
parts.role: Supplies the air stream that lifts the shells.

parts.name: Shell bin
parts.role: Collects cocoa shells, a by-product used as mulch or tea.

parts.name: Melanger stand
parts.role: Holds the motor that turns the granite bed.

parts.name: Granite bowl
parts.role: The stone bed that the rollers grind against.

parts.name: Granite rollers
parts.role: Heavy stone wheels that crush nibs into liquor finer than the tongue can feel.

parts.name: Sugar hopper
parts.role: Doses fine sugar into the liquor.

parts.name: Milk powder hopper
parts.role: Doses milk powder for milk and white chocolate.

parts.name: Conche frame
parts.role: Supports the heated trough and the drive.

parts.name: Conche trough
parts.role: A heated stainless trough where chocolate is kneaded for hours.

parts.name: Conching paddles
parts.role: Stir and aerate the chocolate, driving off acids and water.

parts.name: Gear motor
parts.role: Drives the conche paddles slowly and with great force.

parts.name: Hot-water jacket
parts.role: Copper pipes carry warm water around the trough to hold it at 60–80 °C.

parts.name: Tempering machine
parts.role: Melts, cools and rewarms the chocolate to grow only Form V crystals.

parts.name: Tempering display
parts.role: Shows the working temperature and the crystal form it produces.

parts.name: Tempering kettle
parts.role: A water-jacketed bowl that holds the chocolate during tempering.

parts.name: Agitator motor
parts.role: Keeps the chocolate moving so it tempers evenly.

parts.name: Chocolate pump line
parts.role: Carries conched chocolate to the tempering machine.

parts.name: Heated chocolate main
parts.role: A jacketed pipe that keeps tempered chocolate at its working temperature on its way to the depositor.

parts.name: Depositor gantry
parts.role: A yellow frame that holds the depositor over the conveyor.

parts.name: Depositor hopper
parts.role: Holds tempered chocolate above the pistons.

parts.name: Piston depositor
parts.role: Four pistons, one per cavity, each pushing out exactly 100 g.

parts.name: Conveyor belt
parts.role: Carries the moulds through every station at a steady speed.

parts.name: Conveyor frame
parts.role: Stainless rails and legs that are easy to wash down.

parts.name: Cooling tunnel
parts.role: A chilled, humidity-controlled tunnel at about 12 °C.

parts.name: Chiller unit
parts.role: Refrigeration fans that blow cold air through the tunnel.

parts.name: Flow wrapper
parts.role: Wraps each bar in foil and a paper sleeve at high speed.

parts.name: Foil reel
parts.role: A reel of gold aluminium foil for the inner wrap.

parts.name: Paper reel
parts.role: Printed paper for the outer sleeve.

parts.name: Outfeed conveyor
parts.role: Carries wrapped bars to packing.

parts.name: Shipping carton
parts.role: Cartons of wrapped bars ready for the warehouse.

accuracy: Process temperatures and times follow typical industrial and couverture guidance; exact values vary by recipe and manufacturer. The crystal outcome is a simplified rule based on the Form V working window.
sources: Beckett, Industrial Chocolate Manufacture and Use, 5th ed. (2017)
Afoakwa, Chocolate Science and Technology, 2nd ed. (2016)
Wille & Lutton, Polymorphism of cocoa butter, J. Am. Oil Chem. Soc. 43 (1966)
